title: automate-controlplane-subnet-claiming-with-csr-auth-and-dns-liveness-prober
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: Private control planes often fail during zero-downtime upgrades because controlplane nodes are scheduled into recently-provisioned subnets before route tables, peering, or DNS propagation completes. This PR automates a safer subnet enrollment flow for the installer and introduces a lightweight CSR-based authorization handshake so nodes only join the control plane after a signed enrollment token is present. Additionally, a DNS liveness prober runs as part of the installer to detect stale resolver records and block finalizing controlplane endpoints until DNS checks pass.

Design summary: 1) Subnet claim controller (Terraform + Helm hooks): the installer will mark candidate subnets as CLAIMED by adding tags and storing a claim record in the installer state bucket; a pre-attach validation ensures CIDR and AZ compatibility with existing controlplane topology. 2) CSR enrollment: new installer certificate-signing flow issues short-lived bootstrap CSRs; controlplane node agents call the CSR endpoint and receive a signed enrollment certificate only after the claim controller validates the subnet and provisioning signals (NAT/route/endpoint health). 3) DNS liveness prober: a small Go probe deployed as a Job that validates controlplane resolver records (both authoritative and cross-account forwarding where applicable) across configured regions and emits Prometheus metrics and verbose logs for troubleshooting. 4) Rollout: default is opt-in for existing customers via helmValues.install.enrollment.enabled=false; new installs opt-in=true.

Files & surface area: terraform/modules/subnet-claim (new) with state locking support; helm/controlplane/templates/enrollment-hook-job.yaml; installer/agents/csr-server.go (new, with 500-line test harness); installer/upgrade/rollback orchestrator changes to delay finalization until prober success; tests/integration/subnet-claim-e2e.go (new harness that simulates cross-account forwarding).

Migration & backward compatibility: Existing clusters without enrollment remain unaffected by default. When enabled during upgrades, the orchestrator will do a staged handoff: 1) mark new subnets as CLAIM_PENDING, run DNS prober; 2) if prober passes and CSR handshake succeeds, change to CLAIMED and allow node joins; 3) otherwise, automatically roll back the claim and keep instances in fallback subnets. This avoids split-brain between old/new controlplane nodes.

Security considerations: enrollment CSRs are short-lived (15m) and bound to subnet metadata + instance identity tokens. The CSR signing key is provisioned via KMS and rotated by the platform key-rotation job. All network operations are performed using least-privilege IAM roles scoped to the installer S3/Terraform role.

Testing and CI notes: Added unit tests for CSR validation, Terraform plan checks, and a mocked DNS probe. Integration runs in the perf-canary environment exercise cross-account forwarding and simulate delayed Route53 propagation. CI initially failed on a flaky resolver test; rerun stabilised the job and CI status is now green.

How to verify in staging: 1) helm upgrade --install with values.enrollment.enabled=true and values.enrollment.testMode=true; 2) observe Job "controlplane-dns-liveness" produce PASS metrics; 3) create a subnet claim via terraform apply and verify the installer S3 state file contains the CLAIM_PENDING -> CLAIMED transition; 4) confirm controlplane nodes only register after CSR handshake.

Operational playbook: If a DNS probe stays in FAIL, the orchestrator will mark the claim as failed and emit an incident event to the existing installer alerting topic. Operators can force-override via the 'installerctl claim finalize --force' command after manual verification.

Related work: follows ENG-8342 (subnet lifecycle reconciler) and ENG-8401 (safe upgrade coordinator). See sup ticket SUP-2121 for customer repro that motivated this change.

Review notes: reviewers asked for stronger observability (added per-AZ probe gauges), tightened CSR TTL, and extra terraform plan guards. The PR was squashed on merge.
commits: add: terraform module subnet-claim with state lock and tagging
feat: helm job for dns liveness prober + metrics
feat: csr enrollment server and bootstrap flow
chore: integration tests for cross-account forwarding and prober
fix: orchestrator delay logic and rollback path
release_notes: Automated subnet claiming with optional CSR-based enrollment and DNS liveness gating. Opt-in for existing clusters; enabled by default for new installs. Improves safety for controlplane upgrades and reduces incidents caused by premature node joins.
